set.descent_text: Much of the route can be downclimbed if Adamant is the only goal, and a few rappels can shortcut the long diagonal ramp by going straight from the top of the technical climbing to a point on it. The other option is to go west from the summit to the Adamant-Turret col (easy fifth class or a short rappel) and rappel the steep ice and snow over the bergshrund onto the upper Turret Glacier. That glacier is steep and heavily crevassed, so it is not the casual way down. Parties continuing the traverse go on over Turret toward Austerity instead.
set.approach: From the Fairy Meadow hut, ascend the Granite Glacier until you reach the Turret Glacier. Where crevasses and icefalls allow, step onto the Turret Glacier on either flank of the nunatak, then keep to its left side along the base of Adamant's north ridge. The Kaufman route leaves to the left beneath a prominent triangular snow patch; this variation starts higher up, once above the ramp, by crossing the bergshrund onto easy ice and rock.

review.notes: Approach and descent options from the route page; the Adamant-Turret col descent also matches the traverse page.

set.descent_text: The traverse finishes by going down the Austerity standard route to the Granite Glacier. Austerity's standard route goes down the west ridge, mostly by downclimbing the broken, low-angle rock; short steeper steps can be rappelled with a short rope, but the rock is too broken for long rappels. The ridge leads to the col between Austerity and Ironman, a good bivouac spot. From the col, the steep snow and ice slope can be downclimbed or rappelled, and the bergshrund below it has to be crossed from above without a chance to scout it, so someone in the party should know the way. Beyond it, follow the upper Granite Glacier down through the crevasses toward Fairy Meadow.
set.approach: From the Fairy Meadow hut, go up the moraine to the Granite Glacier and then up the left side of the Turret Glacier until you can step onto the north ridge of Adamant. The climbing starts from there on the ridge crest.

review.notes: Traverse description and Austerity descent details; the ending agrees across three pages.

set.descent_text: Austerity's standard route goes down the west ridge, mostly by downclimbing the broken, low-angle rock; short steeper steps can be rappelled with a short rope, but the rock is too broken for long rappels. The ridge leads to the col between Austerity and Ironman, a good bivouac spot. From the col, the steep snow and ice slope can be downclimbed or rappelled, and the bergshrund below it has to be crossed from above without a chance to scout it, so someone in the party should know the way. Beyond it, follow the upper Granite Glacier down through the crevasses toward Fairy Meadow.
set.approach: Leave Fairy Meadow on the path over the moraine to the Granite Glacier, then cross the fairly flat but crevassed glacier beneath Pioneer and Adamant. Pass below the lower northeast ridge of Austerity and, somewhere under its northwest ridge, thread through the crevasses into the basin between that ridge and the north ridge of Ironman. Climb the basin to the bergshrund below the steep slope leading to the Ironman-Austerity col, which is where the technical climbing begins.

review.notes: Route page for approach and descent; descent matches two other pages.

set.descent_text: Once the snow has melted, go down the west face, slightly right of where the snow patches sit in the photos. It is very steep grass and scree with some slabs, and it is a poor choice when wet. The big scree gully crossed near the top of the ridge is not an option, since it cliffs out part of the way down. Afterward, walk back along the foot of the ridge to Fairy Meadow.
set.approach: Starting at Fairy Meadow, ford to the south bank of Swan Creek and work through woods and some wet ground to the rock and boulders at the foot of the northwest ridge. Scramble a class 3 scree gully to reach the ridge fairly low down.

review.notes: Descent by the west face matches the traverse page; approach from the route page.

set.descent_text: Rappel back down the east face to the base. Cross the moat and walk down the snowfield toward the Friendship Col trail and the hut.
set.approach: From the Fairy Meadow hut, follow the path toward Friendship Col and the Echo Glacier. Gog is the higher, closer-to-the-col summit of the Gog-Magog pair, and the route starts on its east face, reached by hiking across the snow below it and crossing the moat to the rock.

review.notes: Approach toward Friendship Col agrees on both pages; descent is the rappel line stated on the route page.

set.descent_text: Descent is by rappel. From the summit go down the west face to the belay ledge below the wide crack, then rappel the first pitch back down to the notch and the east side. Cross the moat and walk back down the snowfield toward the hut.
set.approach: From the Fairy Meadow hut, follow the path toward Friendship Col and the Echo Glacier. Gog is the closer of the pair to the col and Magog is to its right. Hike across the snowfield to the east face and cross the moat to rock below the notch between the two summits.

review.notes: Route page gives both the approach and the rappel descent.

set.descent_text: From the Horn summit, look for the large rocks and horns at the top of the face where the angle drops to class 3; they make good rappel anchors. A rope of about 50 m gets you down the SE face, and a shorter one may need a bit of downclimbing or one more short rappel to reach the class 3 slopes below. Scramble those back to the Horn-Unicorn col. For Unicorn, a large block on the summit can be slung for a rappel down the SE face, followed by some class 4 downclimbing to easier class 3. From the col, retrace the approach to the Granite Glacier.
set.approach: From Fairy Meadow, go up the moraine and onto the Granite Glacier toward the Horn-Unicorn col. At a suitable point swing right onto the loose class 3 rock and scramble up to the col between Horn on the west and Unicorn on the east. The SE face and east ridge of Horn start from the col or just below it.

set.descent_text: Scramble the ridge from the north summit over the main summit to the south summit, mostly third and fourth class with the odd low fifth move. Descend the southeast ridge by two rappels, the first about 30 m down the ridge, then a longer one down the face. With a single rope, plan on a few shorter rappels along the ridge. Return to the basin below.
set.approach: From the Fairy Meadow hut, follow the Friendship Col trail until it turns up the snow slopes toward Gog and Magog, then continue straight over the ridge, drop down and around the left side of the lake, and climb back up to the base of Quadrant's north face. There is some snow on the approach. The climb begins in an obvious corner above a narrowing chimney; a weakness in the cliff band below can be scrambled directly.

review.notes: Descent over the south summit appears on both Quadrant pages; approach from the route page.

set.descent_text: The usual way down is a variant of the standard route: from the summit, descend toward the Austerity-Ironman col and rappel to the upper Granite Glacier at a spot somewhat east of the col. Along the ridge, the broken low-angle rock is mostly downclimbed. The col is a good bivouac spot. Once on the upper Granite Glacier, follow it down through the crevasses toward Fairy Meadow.
set.approach: From the Fairy Meadow hut, go onto the Granite Glacier and follow it to the Turret Glacier. The Turret Glacier is heavily crevassed and needs careful route-finding; a high camp on the Granite Glacier cuts the effort. The east face is reached from the upper Turret Glacier, where avalanches coming off the face above are a concern.

review.notes: East face route page; its descent is a variant of the standard route covered on two others.

set.descent_text: Descend the standard route on the east snowfields to Friendship Col, then follow the glacier and trail back to Fairy Meadow.
set.approach: From Fairy Meadow, follow the glacier beyond Pioneer Pass, then curve around to the buttress's west side. A snow slope leads to a notch in the ridge, where the climbing starts.

review.notes: Both pages send parties down toward Friendship Col; approach from the route page.

set.descent_text: Scramble down rock to the saddle separating the main summit from the north peak, then drop east, toward Fairy Meadow, on rock and snow. Cross a bergshrund and walk the crest of the east ridge down to the Granite Glacier, then return to the hut.
set.approach: From Fairy Meadow, cross onto the lower Granite Glacier and move west below the icefall, then gain height on glacier and snow to the right of Colossal's east ridge. Continue to the level basin under the saddle that separates Colossal from Enterprise, then angle left toward the couloir on the east face. The route starts at the bergshrund.

set.descent_text: Downclimb the Austerity standard route to the Austerity-Ironman col, an excellent bivouac site, then continue down the standard route onto the upper Granite Glacier. Someone in the party should already know this descent. Broken low-angle rock along the ridge is mostly downclimbed, and the steep snow and ice slope below the col can be rappelled or downclimbed before the bergshrund and the crevasses of the glacier.
set.approach: From Fairy Meadow, climb into the upper Granite Glacier and then into the glacial amphitheater between the northeast and northwest ridges of Austerity's north ridge. The route starts by crossing the bergshrund a few rope lengths left of the snow and ice gully that gives access to the ridge. Early season conditions are best here.

review.notes: Route page; descent matches the standard route page.

set.approach: From the Fairy Meadow hut, head up toward the lower Echo Glacier and pass below the small lakes on it to reach the notch on the northwest ridge of Quadrant. Dropping a little onto the east side of the ridge leads past the Rabbit Ears.

review.notes: Single trip-report style page; only an approach is supported, descent unstated.

set.descent_text: Go down the standard route to the saddle shared by Pioneer and the East Peak of Gothics; the East Peak can be added by a fast party. From that col, follow the glacier back to Friendship Col and then down to Fairy Meadow.
set.approach: From Fairy Meadow, hike toward the Adamant-Austerity glacier, but bear left once past the lower end of Sentinel's north ridge. Continue to Pioneer Pass, the col between Sentinel and Pioneer. Cross the bergshrund and climb the high-angle snow or ice to the pass; the east ridge is gained from there by heading right.

review.notes: Route page; descent via Friendship Col also on the NE ridge page.

set.approach: From the Fairy Meadow hut, hike as if going to Friendship Col, then branch right toward the ridge. The line begins on the lowest reaches of the Shoestring Glacier, almost opposite Quadrant's south face, and gains the northern end of Sentinel's north ridge.

review.notes: Single route page; descent not stated.

set.descent_text: From the main summit, continue southeast along the ridge to the south summit, where a rappel anchor is in place. Rappel to skier's left into a blocky alcove, then follow cairns along an exposed third-class traverse back to the ridge crest. A second rappel station leads to a slightly longer rappel to skier's right off the ridge onto grassy ledges. Hike down the basin.
set.approach: The route starts from the basin below Quadrant, immediately right of where the black rib meets the ground, on ramps where the rock is gray with prominent white veins.

review.notes: Route page gives the descent over the south summit, which agrees with the other Quadrant page.

set.approach: Approach as for the south ridge of Quadrant, then veer left toward the foot of the south peak's south face. The first pitch follows a shallow depression a short distance right of where the face is lowest.

review.notes: Single route page; descent not stated.

bc_1_north_faces_from_fairy_meadow_north.skip_reason: The route page says the description may not match the line the guidebook lists; it is flagged as an error and not recommended, so skipped.

bc_1_north_faces_from_fairy_meadow_outpo.skip_reason: The route page carries a 2026 update saying its description and the guidebook's do not appear accurate (notches needing rappels and harder climbing); skipped.
